reason: The bacterial knobs match one resting lymphocyte's recognition proteins, so these pieces look like the start of the response.
expectation: The matching lymphocyte will recognize the bacterial fragments and begin responding.

alternatives.reason: The node may be needed for activation, but the matching pieces are clear enough to try first.

effect: The matching lymphocyte is activated, so I can now follow its growth in the lymph node.
reaction: The matching shapes made the activation easy to follow.
reason: The node's picture says it supports an activated cell as it divides.
expectation: The activated lymphocyte will multiply in the lymph node.

effect: The activated cell produced antibody-making cells and memory cells, so the next step is to make antibodies.
reaction: It's useful to see that the response produces both immediate defenders and memory.
reason: Antibodies are proteins, and earlier chapters showed that amino acids are their building blocks.
expectation: The antibody-making cells will use the amino acids to make antibodies that match the bacteria.

effect: The cells made matching antibodies, which can now be paired with the bacteria.
reaction: The matching shapes make their target clear.
reason: The antibody tips match the knobs on the bacteria, fitting the goal of coating them.
expectation: The antibodies will attach to and coat the bacteria.

effect: The antibodies coated the bacteria, completing that goal. The remaining goal is to give the body immune memory.
reaction: The matching tips made the coating easy to understand.
reason: The antibody-making and memory cells include lasting memory lymphocytes, so connecting them to the body seems like the next step.
expectation: The body will gain immune memory from the memory lymphocytes.

effect: The body now has immune memory: memory lymphocytes can help produce a faster, larger antibody response if the same antigen returns. Both goals are complete.
reaction: The explanation made the purpose of the memory cells clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Growing the activated lymphocyte in the lymph node was most worthwhile: it showed how one matching cell produces both antibody-making cells and memory cells.

leastWorthwhile.text: Connecting the memory cells to the body felt the least informative as an action, although the result explained what memory does.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the same response produces both cells that make antibodies and lasting memory cells.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt entirely arbitrary, though the neighboring immune cells' help with activation was described rather than shown as a separate step.

continue.text: I would probably continue if another chapter offered a similarly clear connection between body structures and what they do. The matching shapes and the memory outcome made this chapter satisfying, though the choices were mostly straightforward.
